d: Conservationists help to protect wildlife from the city of Cape Town to the African bush.
The Sun River  a helicopter trip  a trout hatchery  fly-fishing  an old-fashioned cattle drive.
Marine iguanas, giant tortoises and sea lions of the Galápagos Islands.

Meeting people around the world who dedicate their lives to helping animals  translocating a blesbok to greener pastures in South Africa  baboons cross a busy highway  an orphaned baby tapir  a sanctuary for rescued farm animals.
Orphaned orangutans on the island of Borneo  tiger sharks in Fiji  wallabies on the island of Tasmania  pink dolphins in Singapore.
Hanna explores global conservation efforts, meets African elephants, zebras, pygmy hippos, orangutans, dugongs and more on their wildlife journey.

Jack helps return a grizzly bear to a forest in Montana and ventures into the Amazon Rainforest to find some toxic animals  the Hannas head to a horse ranch near Calgary, and they trek into a Bornean jungle to find wild orangutans.

Jack Hanna and his family travel around the world to discover, interact with and learn about some of Earth's most threatened and endangered species and the conservation and protection efforts to save them.
Bighorn sheep on a Canadian roadside  leeches  Australian kangaroos  rare bearded pigs in Malaysia  a puff adder snake.
Jack meets some of the most ancient species living on Earth, including red pandas, hoatzins, koalas, crocodiles and pelicans.
A disappearing civet  a missing elephant  decoding bats.
A countdown celebrating some of the unique animals on Earth, including pink river dolphins, emus, Sichuan takin, okapi, gerenuk and more.
Jack counts down some of his most extreme animal destinations around the world.
